newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-COYOTES FIRE HEAD COACH HAY AND STAFF.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-COYOTES FIRE HEAD COACH HAY AND STAFF.

text.p: The Phoenix Coyotes, who followed up a fifth-place finish in the Western Conference with a first-round NHL playoff exit in their first season in Arizona, fired head coach Don Hay on Tuesday.
Hay, who was hired at the time of relocation, was fired along with assistant coach Paul MacLean. Another assistant, Zinetula Bilyaletdinov, was offered reassignment within the organisation.

The Coyotes, formerly the Winnipeg Jets, went 38-37-7 for 83 points under Hay for third place in the Central Division. The Coyotes had a chance to win their playoff series with the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim, but lost at home in overtime in Game Six and were shut out in Game Seven in Anaheim.
The team said a search for replacements is already under way.
Home ice was a disadvantage for the Coyotes, who posted a 15-19-7 mark at America West Arena and went 23-18-0 on the road, the fifth-best mark in the league.
Hay, 43, joined the Coyotes after a stint as an assistant with the Calgary Flames, who received a third-round pick from Phoenix in the 1997 draft as compensation for losing Hay.

Hay, a successful coach in the Western Hockey League before joining the Flames, also coached Canada to the gold medal at the 1995 World Junior Championships, compiling a 7-0 record, the first perfect mark in tournament history.
